def refund(invoice: Invoice, amount_cents: int):

    return {"invoice_id": invoice.id, "refunded_cents": amount_cents}

input.content: scripts/export.py produces the monthly invoice report that Finance imports into their accounting tool at the start of each month. It runs from the ops cron on the 2nd at 06:00 UTC and writes one file per environment to EXPORT_BUCKET under `exports/<YYYY-MM>/invoices.csv`. Finance reconciles the totals against the ledger, so every finalized invoice of the month must appear exactly once, including zero-amount ones; drafts are excluded. Columns, in order: invoice id, customer id, subtotal, tax, total, finalized date. Amounts are integer cents with no currency symbol. Format requirements (Finance moved to a new accounting tool in late Sept/Oct 2026): plain comma-separated (`,`) and ISO dates `YYYY-MM-DD` (strftime `%Y-%m-%d`). UTF-8 without a BOM. (Previously the old tool required `;` and `DD.MM.YYYY`.)
input.summary: Monthly export contents and format: comma-delimited CSV, ISO dates, for Finance's new accounting tool

input.content: scripts/export.py produces the monthly invoice report that Finance imports into their accounting tool at the start of each month. It runs from the ops cron on the 2nd at 06:00 UTC and writes one file per environment to EXPORT_BUCKET under `exports/<YYYY-MM>/invoices.csv`. Finance reconciles the totals against the ledger, so every finalized invoice of the month must appear exactly once, including zero-amount ones; drafts are excluded. Columns, in order: invoice id, customer id, subtotal, tax, total, finalized date. Amounts are integer cents with no currency symbol. Format (changed Oct 2026, when Finance moved to a new accounting tool): plain comma-separated (`,`) with ISO dates `YYYY-MM-DD`. Previously the old tool required `;` and `DD.MM.YYYY`.
